blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
British humour can surprise newcomers. A lot of it means saying the opposite of what you feel. This is called irony.

Sometimes British people describe something big as if it were small. This is called understatement. If it is raining hard and a colleague says "lovely weather," that is irony. If a big project fails and someone says "that could have gone better," that is understatement.

These jokes are not mean. They are a kind of British friendliness. A quiet, dry joke is often a signal that you are close enough to share a small laugh.

items.q: What is irony, according to the text?
options: Saying the opposite of what you feel
items.why: "A lot of it means saying the opposite of what you feel. This is called irony."

items.q: A colleague says "lovely weather" while it is raining hard. This is an example of…
items.why: Dizer o contrário do que sente ("lovely" na chuva forte) é ironia.

items.q: Which sentence is an example of understatement?
options: "That could have gone better" after a big failure
"This is the worst day of my life!"
items.why: Understatement = descrever algo grande como se fosse pequeno; um grande fracasso vira "could have gone better".

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: A quiet joke can mean you are close to someone.
British irony is always meant to hurt people.
Dry British jokes are usually friendly.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "These jokes are not mean", então o autor discordaria de que a ironia sempre magoa.

items.q: The text suggests that a quiet, dry joke is often…
options: a sign that the person is bored
items.why: Inferência: "a signal that you are close enough to share a small laugh" — a piada discreta é um gesto amigável.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver explicando a piada do gerente a um colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hey, wait a second. I saw your face after the meeting. You looked confused when the manager said "well, that went well."

I know that meeting was terrible. Nothing worked. The client was angry, and the numbers were wrong. So when he said "that went well," he did not mean it. It was a joke. It is called irony — you say the opposite of what is true.

He was not being cruel. This is very British. When something goes badly, they often make a small, quiet joke instead of shouting. His face was calm and serious, but everyone smiled. That calm, serious face is part of the joke. We call it deadpan.

Here is the nice part. He made the joke to you, not only to the team. That means he likes you. British people tease the people they trust. It is a small sign of friendship, not a problem.

So next time, do not worry. When you hear a calm voice say the opposite of the truth, it is probably a joke. Just smile back. You do not need a big laugh — a quiet one is enough. And if you really don't understand, ask. The London team will like that you tried.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did the manager say after the meeting?
items.why: "the manager said 'well, that went well.'"

items.q: Why did the manager say "that went well"?
options: He did not watch the meeting
items.why: "he did not mean it. It was a joke. It is called irony."

items.q: What does "deadpan" mean in the audio?
options: A calm, serious face while joking
items.why: "His face was calm and serious… That calm, serious face is part of the joke. We call it deadpan."

items.q: The audio suggests that the manager made the joke to the colleague because…
options: he likes and trusts the colleague
he wanted to test the colleague
he was angry with the colleague
items.why: Inferência: "he likes you. British people tease the people they trust."

items.q: What does Oliver suggest the colleague should do next time?
items.why: Inferência: "Just smile back… a quiet one is enough."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "He used irony when he said 'nice job' after the big mistake." Irony means…
options: saying the opposite of what you mean
items.why: Irony = ironia: dizer o contrário do que se pensa.

items.q: "After losing the deal, she said 'not our best day.' That is an understatement." An understatement is…
options: making a big thing sound small
items.why: Understatement = eufemismo: descrever algo grande como se fosse pequeno.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He told the joke with a serious, ___ face, and nobody knew if he was joking."
items.why: Deadpan = sério / sem expressão ao fazer a piada.

items.q: "My colleagues like to tease me about my coffee." To tease means…
options: to make friendly jokes about someone
items.why: To tease = provocar / brincar de forma amigável.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He did not laugh loudly; he just gave a small, ___ laugh."
items.why: Quiet laugh = risada discreta, baixa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "After a hard meeting, she said 'that went well' to lighten the mood." To lighten the mood means to…
items.why: Lighten the mood = deixar o clima mais leve, mais relaxado.

items.q: "Don't worry, he was only pulling your leg." This means he was…
items.why: Pull your leg = brincar, mexer com você de forma amigável.

items.q: "I didn't understand the joke at first, but then I got it." To get it means to…
items.why: Get it = entender, sacar a piada.

items.q: "The whole team cracked up at his dry joke." To crack up means to…
items.why: Crack up = cair na risada, começar a rir.

items.q: "He kept a straight face and said 'lovely' in the rain — I couldn't keep a straight face." To keep a straight face means to…
items.why: Keep a straight face = manter o rosto sério, segurar o riso.
